title: Surgical Dressing Study Comparing SYLKE vs Other Common Incisional Dressings Following Abdominoplasty/Panniculectomy Patients
official: A Randomized Split-Wound Clinical Trial Comparing SYLKE Silk Fibroin Dressing to Standard Adhesive Dressings in Abdominoplasty and Panniculectomy Patients
summary:
Include primary, secondary, and exploratory objectives.

Primary Goal: To compare the effects of a silk fibroin-based dressing versus standard postoperative dressings on scar quality.

Secondary Goal: To compare the incidence of medical adhesive-related skin injuries (MARSIs) in the immediate postoperative period between patients treated with silk fibroin-based dressings and those treated with standard postoperative dressings, and to evaluate long-term wound healing outcomes between groups.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Patients 18 years of age or older

Patients scheduled to undergo abdominoplasty or panniculectomy

The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule

Exclusion Criteria:

Patients under 18 years of age

Patients with a known allergy or sensitivity to silk-based products

Patients with known allergy to Dermabond Prineo
